title: Whole Overcrest Hood and Open Sided Siphon Cutaway
description: One wholly newly authored complete dry longitudinal half-section of an over-crest siphon-spillway-inspired architectural body. A single connected closed material solid includes the entire broad flat ground sole, shaped mass beneath the passage, complete far side wall, continuous thick overhead hood and one integral open summit breather. The real rectangular passage rises from a lower upstream mouth to a flat high summit and then descends to a lower downstream terminal; its complete floor, underside of roof and rear lining remain exposed along one deliberate full-length near-side section. Both entire end mouths are open through the passage, not capped by presentation faces. One genuinely hollow rectangular vent at the summit passes through the finite roof thickness into the main passage and has complete inner walls, outer walls and a finite top rim. No surrounding reservoir, whole dam, flowing water or terrain is supplied. Unlike the old rounded overflow crest and low basin, this body has a roofed rising-and-falling passage and a true open summit branch rather than an unroofed descending apron and basin. Unlike the old bellmouth shaft cutaway, there is no radial funnel or deep vertical shaft turning into a horizontal pipe: this new rectangular route climbs over a longitudinal summit before descending. Unlike the marine returning-pipe apparatus, there is no separate circular pipe, annular pedestal, side pivot, counterarm or weight. Every coordinate and graded closed boundary newly authored together, no old crest, pipe, shaft, vent or model imported, scaled or cut. The material body is one whole connected editable closed mesh with four opaque untextured constant PBR roles, metre-style Z up and the whole horizontal envelope centred over its complete flat ground sole; one model zero scenes. The absent near wall is intentional explanatory sectioning of the complete route, not damage and not a claim of a complete enclosed pressure conduit. Broad siphon-spillway vocabulary only; generic static civil-geometry art, not a named dam replica or engineering design. No hydraulic priming, air-control operation, flow, pressure, capacity, watertightness, water retention, cavitation, flood safety, structural stability, material properties, fabrication, installation or maintenance capability made or verified. No rigging, animation or interaction.
